description: Lattice mechanics for the collapse and orthogonal operators. These rules are how the substrate algebra actually evaluates.

collapse_operator.applies_when: Two assertions a1, a2 share the same (node, property).

refinement.condition: values are in the same chain AND a2.depth > a1.depth
refinement.action: Both kept. a2 is canonical (deeper); a1 becomes a supporting attestation with edge refined_by → a2.
refinement.example: color=red (depth=1) ⊕ color=RGB(220,20,60) (depth=3) → canonical RGB(220,20,60); 'red' kept as attestation

subsumption.condition: values are in the same chain AND a1.depth > a2.depth
subsumption.action: Symmetric to refinement. a1 remains canonical.
subsumption.example: Pantone 199C ⊕ red → canonical Pantone 199C; 'red' kept as attestation

alternatives.condition: values are in the same property at the same depth in different branches
alternatives.action: Both stored. contradicted_by edge created between them. The dossier surfaces both with provenance.
alternatives.example: color=red (depth=1) ⊕ color=blue (depth=1) → both stored, marked contested

incompatible_property.action: TYPE ERROR. Cannot collapse — these aren't talking about the same dimension. Rejected by admission with reason type_mismatch.

enumerated_conflict.condition: both values are at precision_tier='enumerated' AND not equal
enumerated_conflict.action: Hard conflict. No refinement is possible since enumerated values are exact. contradicted_by edge created and the assertion is flagged as a hard contradiction (not a soft one resolvable by deeper data).

orthogonal_operator.applies_when: Two assertions about the same node have different properties.
orthogonal_operator.action: No interaction. Both stored independently. The node's full description is the tensor product over all its property assertions.
orthogonal_operator.example: car.color=red ⊗ car.manufacturer=Ford ⊗ car.origin=Mexico → three independent property chains, all valid

refinement_rules.monotonic_depth: Within a chain, depth strictly increases as you descend. Cannot have a child at the same or shallower depth than its parent.
refinement_rules.cycle_invariant: Every value in a chain has the SAME cycle (the property's cycle). Values cannot change property by being refined.
refinement_rules.parent_uniqueness: Each value has exactly ONE parent (single inheritance). Two parents would force the substrate to pick which property the value belongs to.
refinement_rules.root_per_property: Each property has exactly ONE root value at depth=0, which IS the property concept node itself.

value_normalization.alias_resolution: Common aliases ('crimson' → 'red' alias, not refinement) are stored as aliases on the canonical value, not as separate lattice nodes.
value_normalization.case_insensitive: Value lookup by name is case-insensitive. Display preserves the original casing of the canonical form.
